exercise.name: Band High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension
aliases: Standing band overhead extension facing away

reference.title: Band High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arms straighten, breathe in as the band draws the hands back behind the head.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, short pause, about 2 s back

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower return, a step farther from the rack, then the next band up.

cues.text: Loop the band round a rack upright behind you, above head height. Staggered stance facing away, lean forward a little, trunk braced. Hold the band in both hands behind the head, palms facing, upper arms forward and up beside the head, elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows, pushing the hands forward and up in line with the upper arms; only the forearms move.
Arms straight but not locked hard, upper arms beside the head; squeeze the triceps.
Breathe in and let the band draw the hands back behind the head, keeping the elbows pointing forward.
Short pause with the elbows fully bent, then straighten again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about shoulder width, pointing forward.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging (turning it into a pullover)
mistakes.fix: Hold the upper arms still; move only at the elbows.
Ribs down, slight forward lean, glutes braced.
Let the hands come well behind the head.

kinematics.norm: About 110-120 degrees in the stretch to nearly straight; overhead elbow extension grew the triceps more than the neutral-arm position (Maeo et al. 2022).
Still, forward and up beside the head (clinical opinion)
Anchored high behind so it pulls the hands back toward the stretch; Boehler 2011 compared triceps activity across exercises.
Staggered stance, leaning forward about 15-20 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 1 s out and 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band High Pulley Overhead Triceps Extension, video (movement reference)

Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position (Eur J Sport Sci 2022, DOI 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279; PubMed 35819335; 21 adults, 12 weeks, cable)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Elbow pain: shorten the stretch (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain overhead: lower the upper arms toward horizontal (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: upper arms pointing more forward than up.
regressions: Lighter band or step closer to the rack.
progressions: Stronger band or step farther away.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main mover. With the arms overhead the long head works from a stretched position; overhead extensions grew the triceps more than neutral-arm extensions (Maeo et al. 2022), and the heads share the work differently across the range (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main mover. With the arms overhead the long head works from a stretched position; overhead extensions grew the triceps more than neutral-arm extensions (Maeo et al. 2022), and the heads share the work differently across the range (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades upward with the arms overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades upward with the arms overhead.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk against the band pulling back (clinical opinion).
